checks.name: kernel command line
checks.output: rw quiet splash console=tty0 console=ttyS0,115200 no_timer_check

checks.name: no build override in /usr/local/bin
compositor and shell are installed
runtime libraries resolve
checks.command: for b in amity-comp amity-shell; do ldd "$(command -v $b)" | grep "not found"; done | wc -l

checks.name: start the session on amity-comp
checks.command: systemctl stop amity-session.service; loginctl terminate-user amity 2>/dev/null; sleep 2; systemctl reset-failed amity-session.service 2>/dev/null; date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S" > /run/amity-test-start; systemctl start amity-session.service; sleep 5; systemctl is-active amity-session.service

checks.name: amity-comp is the session compositor
compositor answers on its debug socket
XWayland display is up
shell is running
starts with one output
launch a terminal on the first output
checks.command: cd /home/amity && runuser -u amity -- env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u amity) WAYLAND_DISPLAY=$(basename $(ls /run/user/$(id -u amity)/wayland-? | head -1)) DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix 2>/dev/null | head -1 | tr -d X) DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/$(id -u amity)/bus sh -c 'foot --app-id=term.one >/tmp/foot1.log 2>&1 &'

checks.name: window on the first output
a second output appears when a monitor is connected
the second output is placed to the right of the first
the first output keeps its taskbar; the second has the whole screen as work area
existing windows stay where they are
launch a terminal with the pointer on the second output
checks.command: cd /home/amity && runuser -u amity -- env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u amity) WAYLAND_DISPLAY=$(basename $(ls /run/user/$(id -u amity)/wayland-? | head -1)) DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix 2>/dev/null | head -1 | tr -d X) DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/$(id -u amity)/bus sh -c 'foot --app-id=term.two >/tmp/foot2.log 2>&1 &'

checks.name: new window opens on the second output
and lies inside it
maximize fills the output the window is on
restore
a window can be dragged to the other output
the dragged window moved by the drag distance
maximize there fills the first output work area
restore after the move
and dragged back
launch a third terminal on the second output
checks.command: cd /home/amity && runuser -u amity -- env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u amity) WAYLAND_DISPLAY=$(basename $(ls /run/user/$(id -u amity)/wayland-? | head -1)) DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix 2>/dev/null | head -1 | tr -d X) DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/$(id -u amity)/bus sh -c 'foot --app-id=term.three >/tmp/foot3.log 2>&1 &'

checks.name: third window opens on the second output
it is minimized; focus returns to the window used before
the second window is maximized on the second output
the output disappears when the monitor is disconnected
a maximized window is maximized on the remaining monitor
the first window did not move
the minimized window is still minimized and listed
restoring the window minimized on the lost monitor shows it on the remaining one
and it is fully inside the work area
all three windows are still there
close the terminals
checks.command: pkill -u amity -x foot; sleep 2; pgrep -u amity -x foot | wc -l

checks.name: compositor and shell did not crash or restart
checks.command: journalctl -b --no-pager -o cat -t amity-session --since "$(cat /run/amity-test-start)" | grep -c -E "panicked|RUST_BACKTRACE|the shell exited|the shell closed its channel"; systemctl show amity-session.service -p NRestarts --value

method: root serial console; QMP input-send-event through the virtio keyboard and tablet; compositor state from its development debug socket; QMP screendump
